rows.title: a virtual HDMI output whose EDID declares 3D (frame packing, top and bottom, side by side half) shows the declared pair in each mode
rows.versions_note: ours: Stereo KWin 6.7.4-2+stereo3d58 and Mesa +stereo3d24 of the tree; stock: Debian's kwin-wayland 6.7.4-2+b1 and Mesa 26.1.6-1; the kernel is the edition's 7.3.4-stereo3d18 in both
rows.proves: The compositor lists the 3D modes the EDID declares, sets each one, and the frame scanned out holds the desktop and a 2D client identical in both eyes, the declared client's left view only in the left eye and its right view only in the right eye, a 2D mode's client the same in both eyes (vkms-stereo-bench's kwin phase, analyze-kwin.py).
rows.not_proven: A real television, the HDMI vendor InfoFrame (VKMS has no link), frame packing at other refresh rates, side by side full (needs the DRM core change), a GPU renderer (software Mesa).

rows.title: a plain monitor (no 3D mode) shows one eye of a declared pair, never the pair side by side
rows.proves: In the plain 1920x1080 60 Hz mode the declared client shows its left view only (red, no green) at the place of its 2D part, the desktop and a fullscreen 2D client unchanged.
rows.not_proven: Which eye a person sees on a real monitor beyond the left-eye rule; stock shows nothing of the client: the test client did not appear.

rows.title: an anaglyph output shows the two eyes combined
rows.skip: the output's anaglyph switch has no command line client: kscreen-doctor of the edition (libkscreen knows KScreen::Output::setAnaglyph) has no such setting, and kwinoutputconfig.json with anaglyph true for the output was kept but not applied when KWin started (measured in the lab guest: the frame stayed pure red, blue and black). Needs a small libkscreen client that calls setAnaglyph, then the row compares the client area against the Dubois mix of the two views.

rows.title: a deep colour ramp keeps its levels to the output (10, 12 and 16 bits)
rows.skip: the deep-colour skill describes the proof (a ramp counted per eye in a deep readback) but has no runnable rig; VKMS scans out AB48 (16 bits per channel), so the readback exists in the screens guest. Needs a ramp client drawn at 16 bits and a counter of distinct levels per eye; not written here.

rows.title: the sound graph follows a 44.1 kHz and a 96 kHz file where the device takes it (stock PipeWire stays at 48 kHz)

cmd: sh /lab/rows/as-rig.sh python3 -I /opt/lab/rig/proof.py rows --devices dac,hdmi --rates 44100,96000 > /evidence/rows.jsonl 2>/evidence/proof.err; python3 -I /lab/rows/audio_judge.py follow /evidence/rows.jsonl
versions: dpkg-query -W pipewire wireplumber sparky-stereo-audio 2>&1; pw-metadata --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

cmd: sh /lab/rows/as-rig.sh python3 -I /opt/lab/rig/proof.py rows --devices dac,hdmi --rates 44100,96000 > /evidence/rows.jsonl 2>/evidence/proof.err; python3 -I /lab/rows/audio_judge.py follow /evidence/rows.jsonl

rows.proves: With a private PipeWire and WirePlumber and fake ALSA devices that take exactly the rates they are told (a DAC with 44.1 to 192 kHz; an HDMI sink with 32 to 96 kHz), a 24 bit file at 44.1 and at 96 kHz makes the graph and the device run at that rate with no resampling; the settings are read from PipeWire (pw-metadata) and the stream nodes (pw-dump).
rows.not_proven: A real sound card, a real HDMI display, the quality of the conversion where the device cannot take the rate, Bluetooth.

rows.title: a 16 bit only device is opened in 16 bit with triangular dither and the graph follows its rate

versions: dpkg-query -W pipewire wireplumber sparky-stereo-audio 2>&1; pw-metadata --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

cmd: sh /lab/rows/as-rig.sh python3 -I /opt/lab/rig/proof.py rows --devices pcm16 --rates 44100,48000 > /evidence/rows.jsonl 2>/evidence/proof.err; python3 -I /lab/rows/audio_judge.py dither16 /evidence/rows.jsonl

rows.proves: A fake device that takes S16_LE only: the device is opened in S16_LE, the sink carries dither.method triangular, the graph runs at the file's rate.
rows.not_proven: That the dither is audible or inaudible; a 16 bit file on a 16 bit device is not bit exact with the dither on.

rows.title: the engine detects a 5.1 analog card
rows.proves: A fixture of the kernel's /proc/asound (an HDA codec with three stereo converters, 44.1 to 192 kHz, 16/24/32 bit) is listed by sparky-stereo-audio detect with its rates and 32 bit; expectation from the fixture's own table.
rows.not_proven: The channel count: the engine reads rates and bits, not channels, so 5.1 is not distinguished from stereo.

rows.title: the engine detects a 16 bit only sound card
rows.proves: A USB audio stream file whose only format is S16_LE, 44.1 and 48 kHz: the engine lists 44100 48000 and says 16 bit only.

rows.title: the engine reads an HDMI sink's EDID audio block (LPCM for the graph, encoded formats for passthrough)
rows.proves: An ELD (the kernel's reading of CTA-861 short audio descriptors) with LPCM 32 44.1 48 96 kHz 16 20 24 bit and AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, DTS-HD and TrueHD (MAT, coding type 12) with other rates: the engine lists exactly the LPCM rates and 24 bit, none of the encoded formats' extra rates (88.2, 176.4, 192 kHz).
rows.not_proven: Passthrough itself: the engine of 0.1.0 does not choose AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS or TrueHD from the EDID (the audio skill says it is still to build); the row proves that the encoded formats' rates do not leak into the graph's list.

rows.title: the engine names a headphone jack as a port type
rows.proves: An analog HDA codec with a pin whose default is [Jack] HP Out: the engine's answer must name the headphone port.
rows.not_proven: The engine of sparky-stereo-audio 0.1.0 reads converters only, never pin default configuration: expected to fail on ours until a later version reads port types (see Faults found).

rows.title: a virtual HID joystick with 128 buttons and 8 axes is seen whole by the kernel and by SDL (stock loses buttons 80 and up)

versions: ls /kern/ours/x/lib/modules; ls /sdl/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ | grep SDL3; zcat /sdl/usr/share/doc/libsdl3-0/changelog.Debian.gz | head -1

rows.proves: In a QEMU guest a UHID device with a report descriptor of 128 buttons, 8 axes and 4 hat switches is created; the kernel's event node (EVIOCGBTNCNT or the key codes), the buttons that arrive when all are held, and SDL3's button, axis counts and held buttons are compared with the descriptor. Ours: the edition's 7.3.4-stereo3d18 with its libsdl3 3.4.18+ds-1+stereo3d4; stock: Debian's 7.3.4+deb14 with libsdl3 3.4.20+ds-1.
rows.not_proven: A real controller, Wine, KDE's game controller page; hats are printed, not judged: hid-input maps all four HID hat switches onto one hat (ABS_HAT0X/Y) on both kernels; the item names uinput, which sets key codes directly and cannot show the 80 button limit of hid-input.

rows.title: a uinput device with 8 axes and 4 hats is seen whole
rows.skip: the uinput route sets axis and hat codes directly, so the kernel and SDL see them whole on stock as well: the row cannot be red on stock, and the loss the item expects is in hid-input (see input-128-buttons); not built as a row
